why: D5. A `companion object`'s members fold onto the enclosing type: `make()` is `java:shop.make.Widget.make`, not `…Widget.Companion.make`. The justification is what call sites actually write — `Widget.make()` from outside and a bare `make()` from inside both name the class, and nothing anywhere writes `Companion`, so a separate node would be a name the graph invented rather than read. The fixture exercises both call forms so they have to land on the same id, and includes a `const val` in the companion because constants fold the same way. `Widget()` inside `make()` is the constructor case: instantiation is a call to the Type.
